:::{#thm-minimum-description-length-maximum-likelihood}
#### Minimum description length and maximum likelihood

Let $x$ be data,
and let $\modelfam$ be a finite set of models that each give $x$ a positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $p(x)$,
with the same codeword length $L$ for every model.
Then a model has the smallest [two-part description length](#def-two-part-description-length) of $x$
if and only if it is a [maximum likelihood estimate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) of the model given $x$.

:::

::: {.proof}

Every model has the first part $L$,
so the models differ only in the second part $\log_2 \frac{1}{p(x)}$.
The function $\log_2 \frac{1}{u}$ decreases as $u$ increases.
So the second part is smallest for the model with the largest $p(x)$,
which is the maximum likelihood estimate.

:::
